title: Exact-Q Graph State-Sum Contraction Evaluators and Machine-Checked Algebraic Kernel for Paths, Binary Trees, and Square Grids
abstract: Motivated by graph state-sum polynomial witnesses Z_{G,q}(X) on paths, binary trees, and square grids in algebraic complexity theory, we present an explicitly scoped, standalone, zero-floating-point verification stack pairing two layers. Layer 1 (ValiantHierarchy.lean, Lean 4.35.0; 18 theorems, 0 sorry, 0 Classical.choice, 0 warnings, 2 zero-axiom theorems) machine-checks four fixed q=2 small-graph contraction identities over Z (3-vertex path P_3 brute-force vs. x^T M z, 4-vertex path P_4 sequential/midpoint/bisection associativity, an 8-term 3-edge 4-vertex degree-3 rooted tree DP factorization, and a 16-term C_4 cycle transfer-matrix trace Tr(ABCD)) alongside 14 elementary integer/Nat/List arithmetic lemmas (q^d <= q^4, list-sum budgets, exponential growth q^{n+1} > q^n, characteristic-free 1- and 2-bit Boolean table selectors, det_2 embedding, integer exponent inequalities n^k < n^{s_1} < n^{s_2} < n^{s_3}, and graph size counts). Layer 2 (VALIANT-HIER-CERT-1.0, pure-stdlib Python Fraction) provides a fully specified four-mode auditor that evaluates general finite-order path ABP/bisection, complete binary-tree bottom-up DP, and square-grid transfer-matrix state sums over Q without floats, replays 16/16 canonical certificates in 0.049-4.319 ms (contracting 5x5 grids over 2^40 states in 4.806 ms), cross-checks all evaluators against brute-force q^E summation, and rejects 54/54 live adversarial attacks.
